senses.gloss: If something is slow, it does not happen in a short time.
If you slow someone or something, he, she, or it does not move as quickly as he, she, or it did before; you lower the speed of something.
If you slow, you do not progress as quickly as you did before.
A slope is one side of a hill.
examples: We will have to climb up this slope to get to the top of the hill.

senses.gloss: The slope of a line is how far up it goes divided by how far along it goes.
If something slopes, it goes either up or down.
examples: The hill slopes down at this point.

senses.gloss: A long thing is slanting when one end is higher up than the other end and also further along. To be on an angle or sloping.
examples: The piece of wood is slanting from the ground up to the door so that a cart with wheels can roll up it.

senses.gloss: A slant is the way a long thing is when one end is higher up and further along than the other end. The way a ramp is.
When something slides, or moves a small distance while touching what it's on, we say it slips.
examples: The hat slipped down until it covered her eyes.

senses.gloss: When someone or something moves without wanting to move, we say it slips.
examples: My foot slipped when I stepped on some ice, and I almost fell.

senses.gloss: A slip is a small mistake.
A slip is a piece of clothing like a small white skirt, that a woman sometimes wears hidden under her skirt or dress.
The sky is what you see when you look up when you're not inside. It's blue with clouds in it. At night it's black with stars in it.
examples: The night sky was full of stars.

senses.gloss: If something is symbolic, it has or is used as a symbol.
examples: In many religions, the number 3 has a symbolic value.
The apology was purely symbolic and did nothing to change the situation.

senses.gloss: A strong soft material that cloth is made of. A certain type of silk worms make it.
examples: This shirt is made of silk.

senses.gloss: A flat thing with a few words or pictures on it to tell people something.
examples: I saw a stop sign, so I stopped the car.

senses.gloss: When someone signs a piece of paper, they write their signature on it.
examples: They signed a contract saying exactly who would do the work and how much money they would be paid.

senses.gloss: If a company signs someone, they hire them to work.
A side is a straight edge of an object.
examples: A square has four sides.

senses.gloss: A side is the left part or the right part of something.
examples: This car has only one door on each side.

senses.gloss: (usually with "with") To side with someone is to be in an alliance with them.
examples: Who will you side with, Bob or Rachel?

senses.gloss: When someone moves a door so that people can't go through it, the person is shutting the door. When someone puts their lips together so that no air or food can go in or out of their mouth, the person is shutting their mouth.
examples: The wind was too cold, so I shut the window.

senses.gloss: Two shoes are two things that someone wears on their feet. Shoes have a hard, flat bottom.
If you shoe, you put shoes on your feet. We usually use this verb as a past participle: We say say someone is shod if they have shoes on their feet.
examples: He was dressed and shod, ready to go out.

senses.gloss: If you shoe a horse, you put horseshoes on the horse.
A shock is the way it feels when a heavy thing suddenly hits another thing.
A shock is a sudden change that surprises people.
Someone is shocked when they are surprised at something
examples: He was shocked at how much she had changed since he had last met her.

senses.gloss: If someone has been shocked, they got a painful feeling due to electricity flowing through their body.
A shelf is a flat thing that people can put books or other things on when they are not using them.
Someone feels shame when they know they did something wrong.
examples: The boy felt shame and gave back the candy he had taken.

senses.gloss: If you shame someone, you make them feel shame.
To shake is to move from side to side many times quickly.
examples: She shook the bottle to mix the drink.

senses.gloss: A shake is a type of beverage.
examples: They were known for their shakes.

senses.gloss: A shake is when something shakes.
A shade is a shadow of a tree or another big thing that blocks some of the light and heat of the Sun.
examples: She rested in the shade of the tree because she felt hot.

senses.gloss: A shade is the slight difference between colors.
If something is shaded, it is shielded from light.
examples: The old tree shaded the animals from the sun.

senses.gloss: If something is shading, it is approaching something slightly.
examples: The grassland was green, shading towards brown in the drier areas.

senses.gloss: When an army stops fighting and lets the other side win, we say that the army surrenders. Sometimes people wave a white flag to show that they are surrendering.
To submit to a person who has more power.
A surrender is the act of surrendering.
If something is sustainable, it can be continued for a long time, especially without using up resources.
examples: The oil-based lifestyle of today is not sustainable.
The government is trying to balance sustainable development with economic growth.

senses.gloss: A substitution is the act of replacing one person or thing with another.
examples: The accidental substitution of one medicine for another can be deadly.
They had no extra players, so were unable to make any substitutions.

senses.gloss: ordinal sixtieth) Sixty is the number that is after 59 and before 61.
examples: There are sixty seconds in a minute and sixty minutes in an hour.

senses.gloss: The number 60.
examples: Sixty is ten less than seventy and ten more than fifty.

senses.gloss: To be 60 years old.
examples: My father is sixty.

senses.gloss: ordinal sixteenth) Sixteen is the number that is after fifteen and before seventeen. It can also be written as 16.
examples: Sixteen persons fit in this small bus.

senses.gloss: The number 16.
examples: Six and ten makes sixteen.

senses.gloss: A set of sixteen things or persons.
examples: These sixteen are very beautiful stones.

senses.gloss: ordinal seventeenth) Seventeen is the number that is after sixteen and before eighteen. It can also be written as 17.
examples: Seventeen birds sit on the roof.

senses.gloss: The number 17.
examples: Seven and ten makes seventeen.

senses.gloss: A set of seventeen things or persons.
examples: The seventeen were leaving the city.

senses.gloss: A servant is someone who works for a person or for a family, doing things like cooking and washing. Often the servant lives in the house where they work. A servant works for the same family all day.
examples: This rich family has three servants working for them in their big house.

senses.gloss: A problem or situation is serious if it is not funny or comical, but important.
examples: This is a serious problem. We must do something.

senses.gloss: A person is serious if the person is not laughing or joking, but saying what they mean.
examples: I see. When you said the room was empty, you were serious!
The woman's face looked serious, so I knew she was saying something important.

senses.gloss: Sense is any basic ability or understanding.
examples: She has a great sense of fashion.
She uses good sense when choosing her friends.

senses.gloss: Sense is the ability to understand a situation or emotions.
examples: I sensed you were upset before you said anything.
I sense you don't want to be with me.

senses.gloss: The way something seems to be is the way you think it is when you look at it, hear about it, think about it, etc.
examples: It seems unlikely that they will remember your name after meeting you once.
As odd as it may seem, the girl's best friend is an eighty year old man.

senses.gloss: To send something is to make the thing go somewhere without the person. A person sends a letter by putting it in a mailbox. A person can send another person somewhere by telling the person to go there.
examples: She needed to send a letter to her mother to say she had arrived safely.
Could you send Roger into see me please?

senses.gloss: A person makes a selection when a person chooses a smaller number of things from a larger group of things.
A selection of things is different things that have been chosen or that you can choose from.
examples: The window of the store shows a selection of the things you can buy in the store.

senses.gloss: A seed is a small round thing that can grow to be a plant, a flower or a tree.
examples: She put the seeds into the ground in the garden so that food and flowers would grow.

senses.gloss: The seed of a man is his semen.
To plant seeds in an area.
examples: I'm going to seed the garden so vegetables grow there.

senses.gloss: If a man seeds in a woman, he ejaculates inside her during sexual intercourse.
You see something when you look at it with your eyes.
examples: She turned her head up and saw clouds in the sky.
I can't see the words in this book because the writing is too small and I don't have my glasses.

senses.gloss: If you are seeing someone, you are dating them.
examples: Me and Katie have been seeing each other for a few months.

senses.gloss: A diocese; a region of a church, generally headed by a bishop, an archbishop or a cardinal
The office of a bishop or archbishop or cardinal.
examples: Venice is the see of a cardinal.
The Pope is the bishop of the see of Rome.

senses.gloss: A screw is a small metal thing for holding pieces of wood together. You turn it to move it in or out of the wood.
examples: I need some screws to hold the shelf to the wall.

senses.gloss: If you screw in a screw, you put it into a piece of wood by turning it.
examples: I screwed the hinge into the door.

senses.gloss: If you say, "screw this", you decide not to do it because you are frustrated.
examples: Screw this, I will just sit here and do nothing all day.

senses.gloss: A pair of scissors is a tool for cutting, with two parts like two knives that move. Scissors are usually used for cutting paper.
The scale of something is its size or level.
examples: It's hard to understand the scale of the change.

senses.gloss: A scale is a small machine for measuring (finding out) how much something weighs (how heavy the thing is.)
examples: She stood on the scale and found out she weighed 150 pounds.

senses.gloss: If you scale something, then you climb up it.
The scope of a book, a law, a duty, etc. is how much is included or how far it can go.
examples: The small budget has limited the scope of the research.
There are plans to expand the scope of the department's activities.

senses.gloss: A scope is an instrument for looking at things, e.g., a telescope or a microscope.
If you scope something (out), you look at it carefully.
examples: I scoped out the place last week. It seems nice.

senses.gloss: A subsidiary is a company that is owned by a larger company. {[ant|parent}}
examples: This company owns three subsidiaries that make different kinds of machines.

senses.gloss: If something is subsidiary, it is connected, but lower in importance, rank, or level, etc.
examples: Surprisingly, the subsidiary company became more successful than the parent company.
At some point work became subsidiary to music for her.

senses.gloss: If you save something, you keep it; you do not give it or toss it away.
examples: Please save that book for me.

senses.gloss: If you save someone, you keep them safe or help them survive.
examples: You saved my life.

senses.gloss: A save is when something was saved. This term is used in sports.
examples: Due to a great save at the end, the game ended 0:0.

senses.gloss: All of x save y describes only that part of x that is not y.
examples: The night air was still and silent save for the voice of a female dispatcher over his police radio.
All my cats are white, save one.

senses.gloss: When you sell something to someone, you give something to someone and the person will give you money for it.
examples: I sell good shoes for a small amount money.

senses.gloss: A person
examples: I heard someone at the door.
You should ask someone who knows more about it.

senses.gloss: A sacrifice is something that a person gives up in order to help him or somebody else. A person who makes a sacrifice for a friend will do something that he might not want to do in order to help his friend.
A sacrifice is an offer given as a gift to a god.
examples: People in the Old Testament offered a lamb as a sacrifice to God for forgiveness.

senses.gloss: If you sacrifice someone or something, you give them up for other things.
The plural form of second; more than one (kind of) second.
examples: The clock shows the seconds.

senses.gloss: A second serving of food for one person.
examples: I'm so hungry that I'm going back for seconds.
This tastes so good. I hope there's enough for us to have seconds.

senses.gloss: Seconds is the present third person singular of second.
examples: If Bill seconds the motion, I'll vote for it.

senses.gloss: If something is straightforward, it is simple. It is easy to understand and easy to know how to do it.
examples: The instructions for how to put this desk together are straightforward.
What we need to do now is straightforward.

senses.gloss: A sphere is a shape that is round in all directions, like a ball. Every point on a sphere is the same distance from the centre (a point in the middle) of the sphere.
examples: The Earth is almost exactly a sphere.
A drop of water can be a sphere while it's falling.

senses.gloss: A simulation of an event is when people make something that looks like the event happening, but it isn't real.
examples: Before we watched them land on the moon, we watched a simulation so we would know what it would look like.
Doctors sometimes learn surgery in a simulation of a real operation.

senses.gloss: Savoury means "not sweet". Food that is savoury does not taste sweet. The savoury course of a meal may have meat or fish and vegetables. This may be followed by a sweet course (called "pudding" or "dessert").
"Savour" can also mean the characteristic taste of something. It can also mean to enjoy something: "He savoured every moment of it".
If you set something somewhere, you put something into a place.
examples: She sets the lamp on the floor.
I was setting glasses on the table when I heard a noise.

senses.gloss: If you set something, you put it into some state or condition.
examples: After changing the batteries, you have to set the clock again.
They set the house on fire

senses.gloss: Something that is set is fixed. It cannot be changed easily.
examples: Don't argue! The rules are set.
The time for the race is set.

senses.gloss: To be ready for something.
examples: Are you set?

senses.gloss: The set is the scenery for a theatrical work such as a play, ballet, musical, etc.
examples: The Metropolitan Opera's set for Aida is spectacular.
I was painting a wall on the set when the director arrived.

senses.gloss: A set is a group of things that are similar or can be used together.
examples: This chess set is too expensive to play chess with it.
I have a set of porcelain figurines depicting characters from Shakespeare's plays.

senses.gloss: When someone uses the word "so-called" to talk about something, they mean that other people talk about the thing that way, but they don't agree.
examples: When are we going to leave this so-called party? (The person saying this thinks it should not be called a party. Probably they think the party is not fun.)

senses.gloss: You use solely to say that somebody or something is the only one like that or that did it.
examples: It is not good for a country to rely solely on one energy source.
You are solely responsible for this problem.

senses.gloss: If you submit something, usually a piece of writing, you give it to somebody to be checked or accepted.
examples: They submitted their final report together with recommendations to the president.
Students will submit their application with examples of work already done by March 31.

senses.gloss: If you submit to some authority, you accept that they have power over you.
examples: At least up to 1985, the British government submitted to the threat of violence from the terrorists.
Although most people submit willingly to this process, very few of them have any choice in the matter.

senses.gloss: a little, not very
examples: What happens in the classroom can be somewhat different from the lesson plan.
She was somewhat surprised to find her name in the morning paper.

senses.gloss: If you survive something, you experience it and you did not die.
examples: They survived the war but died two years later.
Some of the factory's equipment from 1827 still survives.

senses.gloss: Being self-confident is being confident about one's self.
examples: Sally is self-confident, and she thinks that she can do anything.

senses.gloss: A state is a condition or a situation.
examples: I am worried about her. She is in a constant state of depression.

senses.gloss: Any sovereign nation (nation that rules itself) is a state.
examples: The United States is a country with many sovereign nations united with each other.

senses.gloss: To state something is to say it as a fact.
examples: He stated that he hasn't slept in 2 days.

senses.gloss: To state something is to let it be known.
examples: Please state your name and place of business.

senses.gloss: Successive things follow in order, one after another.
examples: Successive governments have refused to make the changes.
Edward Kawak won in four successive years (1982–1985).

senses.gloss: Humor that is not serious but is meant to mimic. Saying something you don't mean, to be funny or to make someone feel bad.
examples: "No, I don't want any food, I'm just standing here holding an empty plate to make my fingers stronger," he said with sarcasm.

senses.gloss: in an important or large enough way
examples: The price of gas dropped significantly today, causing drivers to line up at the pumps to fill up.
His face looked significantly different.

senses.gloss: with a particular meaning
examples: He looked at her significantly.

senses.gloss: Spic is an insulting word for a Latino or Hispanic person.
A schedule is a plan of things that are happening and the times when they happen.
examples: He visits each village in his or her area on a weekly schedule.
The train is right on schedule.

senses.gloss: A schedule is a list, usually one with prices.
examples: Please see the enclosed schedule of costs for facilities and activities.

senses.gloss: If you schedule something, you make a plan for when and where it will happen.
examples: The party was originally scheduled for June 5th.

senses.gloss: If something is supplementary, it is added on; it is not needed, but it is often useful.
examples: Many immigrants are employed but also feel the need to seek supplementary income.
These software solutions are more supplementary than basic.

senses.gloss: The present participle of speak.
The past participle of speak.
examples: I have spoken to her about the car.

senses.gloss: One of many rods that are between the center and outer surface of a wheel.
The past tense of speak.
examples: John spoke to me about his idea.

senses.gloss: The third-person singular form of speak.
examples: I find it difficult to understand him because he speaks with such a heavy accent.

senses.gloss: A student is person who studies a subject, especially in a school.
examples: I am a student at the school.
She is a straight-A student from a good family.

senses.gloss: A student person who is very interested in a subject.
examples: He's a student of the game and can answer any baseball question you ask.

senses.gloss: A study is a formal effort to learn about something, usually with a written report at the end.
examples: A recent study of New Mexico, completed using national survey data, indicates that many older New Mexicans are returning to school.

senses.gloss: If you study something, you make an effort to learn it.
examples: We study math at the school.

senses.gloss: If something is subordinate, it is less important than someone or something else.
examples: Keeping our natural world healthy remains subordinate to the health of the economy.
In society a dominant group often ignores the wishes of subordinate groups.

senses.gloss: A subordinate is someone who is at a lower position in an organization.
examples: A good manager will talk with her subordinates before making most decisions.

senses.gloss: If you subordinate x to y, you give less importance to x and more to y.
examples: When he fell in love, everything else was subordinated to it.

senses.gloss: A scenario is a possible or imagined future, often with detailed plans.
examples: The worst scenario for Nicky, I imagined, would be if Enya suddenly fell in love with another producer.
If the first part can be completed, then two possible scenarios present themselves.

senses.gloss: If you suspend something, you stop it for a time.
examples: The army suspended all operations in the north until the weather has changed.
The conversation was temporarily suspended while everyone watched the TV.

senses.gloss: If you suspend someone from a job or from school, you stop them from going for a time.
examples: Crang was suspended for five games for punching another player.

senses.gloss: If you slather something, you spread a lot of something onto it.
examples: John likes to slather his bread with butter.
I slathered myself with sunscreen before I went to the beach.

senses.gloss: If you slather something, you spread a lot of it onto something else.
examples: John always slathers butter on his bread.
I slathered sunscreen on my skin before I went to the beach.

senses.gloss: The past tense and past participle of send.
ordinal seventieth) Seventy is the number that is after 69 and before 71.
examples: To drive seventy miles per hour is too fast in the city.

senses.gloss: The number 70.
examples: Seventy is ten less than eighty and ten more than sixty.

senses.gloss: To be 70 years old.
examples: My father is seventy.

senses.gloss: When you show something, you make it easy for people to see it.
examples: The clock shows the time of day.
Can you show me your ID?

senses.gloss: A show is a display of art, movie, or drama. It can be a play, a movie, a concert, an opera or a television program.
examples: I saw the art show at the museum.
The show at the movie theater was boring.

senses.gloss: The past participle of show.
When you sit, your body is not standing, but is in a position so that your bottom is on something.
examples: I sit on a chair at the table.
He sat on the ground.

senses.gloss: The past tense and past participle of sit.
If you sing you use your voice to make music.
examples: I'm going to sing a song to you.

senses.gloss: When you stand, your body is at rest and supported only by your feet.
examples: I stand in the bus when there are no seats.
He stood in line at the store for a long time.

senses.gloss: A stand is a position or opinion that you plan to defend and not move from.
You put something on a stand to keep it off the ground or floor.
examples: The clock was on the night stand next to the bed.

senses.gloss: The third-person singular form of stand.

The present participle of stand.
A standing committee, order, etc. is one that is permanent.
The standing of a person is the position or reputation they have in a society or profession.
The standing of a person is the duration they have been in a position.
When you stay somewhere, you do not move from there.
examples: Whenever I am tired I stay in bed.
He stayed at our house for two weeks.

senses.gloss: A stay is a period of time when someone does not move from a location.
examples: He had a stay in the country for a year.

senses.gloss: The past tense and past participle of stay.
examples: I stayed at my friends house last night.

senses.gloss: The third-person singular form of stay.

senses.gloss: An event
examples: Isn't something going to happen?

senses.gloss: Something is a quality that is difficult to identify.
examples: This beer has a certain something that I enjoy.

senses.gloss: If a person says an option, he or she is suggesting.
examples: I suggest that we go to the mall.

senses.gloss: The surface of an object is the outside of the thing.
examples: The surface of the earth is very large.

senses.gloss: The surface of a liquid is the top of it.
examples: The surface of the lake was smooth.

senses.gloss: When a thing surfaces, it comes to the top of liquid.
examples: The fish surfaced to get food.
The swimmer surfaced for air.

senses.gloss: If information or facts surface, they are revealed or become known.
examples: Reports surfaced that claimed the company was under investigation.

senses.gloss: If you are surprised, something that you didn't expect happened.

examples: I lost some weight and now my shirts are a little big.

A spouse is a husband or a wife.
examples: John is my spouse. I married John, in 1999.
Susan is the wife of Paul. She is Paul's spouse.

senses.gloss: The past tense and past participle of shoulder.
The present participle of shoulder.

The way letters are used to write a word; the way a word is spelled.
examples: This page has too many spelling mistakes.
What's the spelling of her last name?

senses.gloss: The present participle of spell.
From a particular time in the past until now or until a later time in the past.
examples: I haven't been there since 1969.
Since you told me about it, I've been thinking a lot.

senses.gloss: You use since to show that something known is the reason for something else.
examples: Since John can't be there, we'll try for another day. (The audience already knows that John can't be there.)

senses.gloss: When you shoot, you use a weapon to throw something at a very fast speed at someone or something.
examples: The man, in a desperate bid for freedom, grabbed his gun and started shooting anyone he could.

senses.gloss: When you shoot something, you photograph or film something.
examples: At the zoo, I like to shoot many pictures of the animals.
The film was mostly shot in France.

senses.gloss: The shoot is the stem or bud of a plant.
examples: The seed I planted yesterday got a tiny shoot.

senses.gloss: A less offensive way of saying shit.
examples: Oh shoot!

senses.gloss: You say shoot when you are angry or in disbelief; to condemn.
examples: Didn't you have a concert tonight? Shoot! I forgot! I have to go and get ready...

senses.gloss: The act of a gun firing.
The sound of a gun firing.

examples: The police are looking for the person responsible for the shooting of a well-known lawyer last night.

senses.gloss: The third-person singular form of shoot.
The plural form of shoot; more than one (kind of) shoot.
The present participle of see.
You use seeing as x, y to show that x is the reason for y.
examples: Seeing there are some new people, maybe we could each introduce ourselves.
We don't think it is a good idea seeing as it will be so expensive.

senses.gloss: You use supposing to talk about an imaginary situation.
examples: Supposing one group practices for one hour and another group practices for two hours, the second group will probably be better.
What would you do, supposing that it really is a ghost?

senses.gloss: The present participle of suppose.
In a strong or powerful way.
examples: John strongly opposes that law. He refuses to change his opinion.

senses.gloss: Stuff is what makes up something; the things that it is made from.
examples: What is all that stuff on your bedroom floor?

senses.gloss: When you stuff something, you put a lot of things inside of it; you compress things into it.
examples: She stuffed the turkey for Thanksgiving using her secret stuffing recipe of diced bread, onions, and celery.

senses.gloss: To be happy and satisfied, usually to do with food.
